title: Lou Chudd's bottom-line dealings; Banashak above the rest
summary: Matassa says Chudd invested only business relationships and underpaid Bartholomew; Banashak was more honest than anyone, majors included.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Mm-hmm. What about his relationship with Lou Chud?

Well, Chud, from what I can tell, didn't invest a lot of personal capital into anybody. I don't mean dollars and cents. I mean relationship capital. Mm-hmm. And I think that even with his enormous support over a long time of Dave Bartholomew, it was all bottom line oriented. Mm-hmm. I may be oversimplifying Lou Chud's personality. But if I had to oversimplify it, I would say it was that. He only invested his friendship and his relationship with people if they meant something to him otherwise in business. That was my experience with him. Right. Okay. And near as I can tell, it certainly was Joe Banaszak's.

I think that he became somebody that it was tough for Joe Banaszak to deal with. Mm-hmm. You know. And I think in the last analysis, even Dave Bartholomew, he didn't treat as well as he might have. He paid Dave lots of money over a long period of time and invested a lot of power in Dave's position. Mm-hmm. But I think even Dave would have to tell you he probably didn't pay him all he should have.
Yeah. Yeah. But I always say, you know, even if, I mean, people at that stratosphere aren't paid, I mean, they're still driving around with… Oh, yes.

Yeah. Nice. It's kind of hard to feel sorry for a guy that buys new Cadillacs regularly and that kind of stuff. It's in a nice house, you know. But I have a kind of feeling about that that's the other way around. Mm-hmm. And the reason I say that is because Luchat also was in that category. He didn't need to skim money from other people. You know. No. So it works both ways, you know. And like I say, it's hard to feel sorry for a guy that's doing real well. But it's also hard to rationalize other people who are doing even better. You know. Yeah. And so who knows. Anyway, that kind of sums, I think, in far too few words, Joe Banaszczak. Because you have to go back and look at… He really worked hard. Mm-hmm. He really worked hard. And he really paid the price wherever it was necessary to do well for people he was working for. Mm-hmm. You know. I mean, I'm not going to say working for any artists.
So you would say he did right, but the artists paid him what…
I would say that if you compared the way he conducted his business with anybody else, that I'm aware of in this business. And you can include the majors.
Include the majors. He stands head and shoulders above them all. He stands above them all.
